scope: Authored educational navigation catalog, NOT clinical research data or patient training data

topics.title: Tiredness and low energy
topics.text: Fatigue, feeling worn out, drained, exhausted or lacking energy during daily activities, even after resting.
topics.description: Fatigue means tiredness or a lack of energy. It has many possible explanations; this page does not identify the cause in your case.
topics.question: What could explain the change in my energy, and what details would help you assess it?
topics.followup: How is your energy different from usual, and what activities are affected?
topics.sourceOrganization: MedlinePlus / U.S. National Library of Medicine

topics.title: Headaches and head pain
topics.text: Pain, aching, throbbing or pressure in the head. Repeated headaches and questions about when head pain happens.
topics.description: Headaches can take different forms. A description of the pattern can help your conversation with a health professional; a reading match cannot identify a headache type.
topics.question: What should I tell you about the pattern of my headaches?
topics.followup: Where do you notice the head pain, and how often does it happen?
topics.sourceOrganization: MedlinePlus / U.S. National Library of Medicine

topics.title: Stomach and digestive concerns
topics.text: Upset stomach, belly discomfort after meals, nausea, bloating, heartburn, constipation, diarrhea or changes in bowel movements.
topics.description: Digestive concerns can involve different parts of the digestive system. This overview is general information, not an explanation for a particular symptom.
topics.question: Which details about my stomach or bowel changes should we discuss?
topics.followup: What digestive change do you notice, and does it seem connected to meals?
topics.sourceOrganization: MedlinePlus / U.S. National Library of Medicine

topics.title: Cough and airway concerns
topics.text: Coughing repeatedly, clearing the throat, a cough that lingers, irritation in the airways and questions about coughing.
topics.description: Coughing is a reflex that helps clear the airways. There are different reasons for a cough; this page does not determine your cause or urgency.
topics.question: What should I tell you about how long I have been coughing and what it feels like?
topics.followup: How long has the cough been happening, and what seems to bring it on?
topics.sourceOrganization: MedlinePlus / U.S. National Library of Medicine

topics.title: Trouble sleeping
topics.text: Difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, waking up at night, poor sleep quality, insomnia or changes in sleeping patterns.
topics.description: Sleep problems can affect sleep quality, timing or duration. This overview can help you prepare questions about your sleep pattern.
topics.question: What information about my sleep pattern would help us discuss this?
topics.followup: Is the difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or something else?
topics.sourceOrganization: MedlinePlus / U.S. National Library of Medicine

topics.title: Worry and anxiety
topics.text: Feeling worried, anxious, nervous, tense or overwhelmed, fear that is difficult to set aside, persistent uneasiness.
topics.description: Anxiety can involve feelings of worry or uneasiness. This educational overview does not diagnose an anxiety disorder or assess mental health urgency.
topics.question: How can I describe the effect that worry is having on my daily life?
topics.followup: When do you notice the worry, and how does it affect your day?
topics.sourceOrganization: MedlinePlus / U.S. National Library of Medicine

topics.title: Diabetes questions and testing
topics.text: Questions about diabetes, blood sugar, A1C tests, family history of diabetes, increased thirst together with frequent urination, or an existing diabetes diagnosis.
topics.description: A health professional uses blood tests to diagnose diabetes. Feeling tired or thirsty alone does not establish diabetes, and this tool does not diagnose it.
topics.question: Would diabetes testing be appropriate for my situation, and how would we interpret it?
topics.followup: Is your question about testing, a previous result, or living with a diagnosis?
topics.sourceOrganization: NIDDK

topics.title: Heart health information
topics.text: Questions about heart disease, heart attacks, chest pressure or discomfort, heart health, or discussing cardiovascular concerns.
topics.description: This CDC page describes heart attack warning signs. Suspected heart attack symptoms need emergency help, not an online questionnaire. This tool does not assess whether a symptom is heart-related.
topics.question: What should I discuss about my heart-health concerns after any immediate care needs are addressed?
topics.followup: For a non-urgent information question, what aspect of heart health do you want to understand?
topics.sourceOrganization: CDC

topics.title: Stroke awareness information
topics.text: Questions about stroke warning signs, sudden trouble speaking, one-sided weakness, facial drooping, or stroke awareness.
topics.description: CDC advises calling 911 immediately for stroke warning signs, including sudden one-sided weakness or trouble speaking. Do not use this tool to decide whether those symptoms can wait.
topics.question: What would I like to understand about stroke awareness after immediate care needs are addressed?
topics.followup: For a non-urgent information question, what do you want to understand about stroke awareness?
topics.sourceOrganization: CDC
